title: Pre-Launch Real Estate Marketing: RERA Rules and How to Run One
seoTitle: Pre-Launch Real Estate Marketing: RERA Rules + Plan
excerpt: What pre-launch means in real estate after RERA, what you can and can't do before registration, a step-by-step EOI campaign plan and a buyer checklist.

faqs.question: What is pre-launch in real estate?
faqs.answer: It is the period before a project's public launch, when developers collect interest from early buyers, often through an EOI, before full prices and inventory are released. Under RERA, a project that must be registered can't be marketed or booked before registration, so a lawful pre-launch runs between registration and the public price launch.

faqs.question: Is pre-launch booking legal under RERA?
faqs.answer: Not before registration. Section 3 of the RERA Act, 2016 bars promoters from advertising, marketing, booking, selling or inviting people to buy units in a project that must be registered until it is registered. After registration, an early-access EOI phase is allowed, within the 10% advance limit of Section 13.

faqs.question: What can a developer do before RERA registration?
faqs.answer: Prepare: creative with space for the RERA details, a landing page on a private link, WhatsApp replies, call scripts, CRM, paused ad campaigns and draft channel partner agreements. Don't run project ads, publish the project page, put up hoardings or collect EOIs before the registration number arrives.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for marketing a project before RERA registration?
faqs.answer: Up to 10% of the estimated project cost under Section 59(1) of the RERA Act. If the promoter keeps breaking the rule or ignores the authority's orders, Section 59(2) allows imprisonment of up to three years, a further fine of up to 10%, or both. State authorities can also order the ads to stop.

faqs.question: Are 'Coming Soon' ads allowed before RERA registration?
faqs.answer: Regulators treat them as advertising. In 2026 Bihar RERA treated 'Coming Soon' posters for an unregistered project as advertising and imposed ₹1 lakh in costs on the developer. Under Section 3, wait for the registration number before any teaser, banner or 'register interest' ad goes public.

faqs.question: Is a pre-launch EOI refundable?
faqs.answer: Only on the terms written in the EOI form. Common terms are a full refund if you don't choose a unit and a deduction if you withdraw after choosing one. Get the refund conditions and timeline in writing before paying.

faqs.question: How should a pre-launch campaign be planned?
faqs.answer: Build creative, the landing page, WhatsApp replies, CRM and paused ad campaigns before registration. On registration day add the RERA details, publish the page and switch ads on. Reply to every enquiry within minutes during the EOI window, then allot units and move ads to site visits after launch.

faqs.question: What should buyers check before paying for a pre-launch offer?
faqs.answer: The project's RERA registration number on the state RERA website, written EOI terms, payment to the developer's account with a receipt, an advance within 10% until an agreement for sale is registered, and a possession date that matches the RERA filing.

faqs.question: Which channels work best for pre-launch real estate marketing?
faqs.answer: Meta ads and lead forms in the project's catchment, Google search ads for the locality and builder name, a project landing page with RERA details, instant WhatsApp replies, briefed channel partners and hoardings near the site. Measure site visits and EOIs by source, not just enquiries.
